notes.reason: The words are Scott's own. Pritchard's post never names the Hadza or any country, she only writes about "foraging peoples today" and "hunter-gatherers", so "the ancestors of the Hadza people on the Kenyan savannah 10,000 years ago" is Scott's gloss, not a paraphrase of her. The note is right: the Hadza live in northern Tanzania around Lake Eyasi, and Survival International, Wikipedia, National Geographic and the Max Planck Institute all say Tanzania; no source places any Hadza in Kenya. But the country plays no role in the argument. Scott's point is that the happiness collapse happened when hunter-gatherers became subsistence farmers and that Pritchard is doing a "bait-and-switch" from that to Mamdani versus Buttigieg; every word of that reads the same with Tanzania in place of Kenya, and a reader who came away believing the Hadza are Kenyan would hold a wrong belief that changes nothing about the post. The review rules say a tangential detail that does not change the argument is pedantic and pedantic notes are bad, so I mark it bad rather than leave the call to Nathan. The correction itself is safe and Scott would probably fix the word if told, but sending a public note over a one-word geographic slip in an aside spends goodwill on nothing.
